taxpayer.notes: Requesting spouse in stand-alone sec. 6015(e)(1) innocent spouse case; civil engineer; married to Zemzem Bedada (nonrequesting spouse) during 2017; separated July 18, 2018; divorced Jan. 22, 2021.

adjustments: no notice of deficiency; IRS assessed additional tax of $5,602 on March 2, 2020 for unreported income ($19,495 petitioner items, $679 spouse dividends)
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Denial of innocent spouse relief under sec. 6015(b), (c), (f) (final determination June 1, 2021)

findings_of_fact.fact: Married to Zemzem Bedada in 2017; separated July 18, 2018; divorced Jan. 22, 2021
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner and Ms. Bedada separated on July 18, 2018. A Judgement of Absolute Divorce was entered on January 22, 2021.

findings_of_fact.fact: Joint 2017 return omitted petitioner's wages $15,625, his unemployment $3,870, and spouse's qualified dividends $679
findings_of_fact.snippet: did not include petitioner’s wages of $15,625 from Sheladia Associates, petitioner’s unemployment compensation of $3,870, or Ms. Bedada’s qualified dividends of $679

findings_of_fact.fact: Return showed overpayment $12,936; after $216 offset, refund of $12,720 deposited to joint account April 24, 2018
findings_of_fact.snippet: After respondent applied an overpayment credit offset of $216, a refund of $12,720 was issued to petitioner and Ms. Bedada on April 24, 2018.

findings_of_fact.fact: $3,389 transferred from joint account to Ms. Bedada's account July 6, 2018
findings_of_fact.snippet: On July 6, 2018, $3,389 was transferred from the joint account to Ms. Bedada’s personal bank account.

findings_of_fact.fact: Additional tax of $5,602 assessed March 2, 2020; Form 8857 filed March 13, 2020
findings_of_fact.snippet: On March 2, 2020, respondent assessed2 additional tax of $5,602.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner knew of Ms. Bedada's income (W-2 and health-related benefit)
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner also indicated that he had knowledge of Ms. Bedada’s income as a “W–2” and a “health-related benefit.”

findings_of_fact.fact: Ms. Bedada granted sec. 6015(c) relief Nov. 27, 2021
findings_of_fact.snippet: On November 27, 2021, she was granted relief for the year in issue under section 6015(c).

findings_of_fact.fact: 2020 overpayment offset of $2,633 applied to 2017 on April 15, 2021
findings_of_fact.snippet: On April 15, 2021, the overpayment from tax year 2020 was offset by $2,633 and applied to the underpayment for the year in issue.
The total amount of unreported income was $20,174. The amount attributable to petitioner is $19,495, approximately 97% of the total unreported income.

findings_of_fact.fact: Account placed in currently-not-collectible (not hardship) status; nothing shows economic hardship
findings_of_fact.snippet: There is nothing in the record from which to conclude that denying relief would cause economic hardship.

findings_of_fact.fact: Divorce decree silent on tax obligations
findings_of_fact.snippet: The divorce decree is silent as to legal obligation to pay any taxes, interest, or penalties

findings_of_fact.fact: No significant benefit; petitioner compliant with tax laws; no poor health asserted
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner is in compliance with the income tax laws and was placed in currently not collectible status not due to hardship.

issues.question: (Innocent spouse, sec. 6015(b)/(c)) Is petitioner entitled to relief under sec. 6015(b) or (c) for 2017?
issues.holding: No; petitioner had actual knowledge of the items giving rise to the liability
issues.computable_reason: Statutory bar follows from found actual knowledge of the omitted items (and 97% of the liability is petitioner's own items)

issues.question: (Innocent spouse, sec. 6015(f) equitable relief) Is petitioner entitled to equitable relief under sec. 6015(f) for 2017?
issues.holding: No; threshold met only for the ~3% attributable to Ms. Bedada; no streamlined relief (knowledge); factors: marital status and compliance favor petitioner, knowledge favors respondent, rest neutral; not inequitable to hold him liable
issues.computable_reason: Facts-and-circumstances weighing of Rev. Proc. 2013-34 factors; threshold attribution (97%/3%) is mechanical but final outcome is discretionary

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent.
decision.summary: Innocent spouse relief under 6015(b), (c), (f) denied for 2017

notes: Stand-alone sec. 6015(e)(1) petition, not a deficiency case; de novo review on administrative record plus newly discovered evidence (sec. 6015(e)(7)). Some facts stipulated. Basis for $5,602 assessment not in record (fn. 2). Petitioner testified credibly he did not review the return carefully but knew of the item. Derived: $19,495 = $15,625 + $3,870; $20,174 = $19,495 + $679.
